The petitioners apprehending their arrest in a case registered in Cr.No.258/2022 by Varthur Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC are before this Court in this petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
seeking anticipatory bail.

2. In the complaint lodged by one Pampa Robin it is averred that her marriage was held on 10.04.2017 with accused No.1 and after her marriage, she was forced to convert to Christianity and baptized on 17.05.2017 and after conversion, her marriage reception was held on 18.06.2017 in Kerala and the entire expenses were met by her.
Her husband was working at Sabre Company situated at ITPL, Bangalore and she was working prior to her marriage at Society General.

sentences.text: Even during her pregnancy she was physically abused.
She gave birth to a female child on 11.10.2019.
Her husband pledged her gold ornaments to meet the hospital expenses.
She had to resign from her job as she was not able to perform well because of the personal issues between her and her husband and her husband did not support her financially etc.
In the month of August 2021, a flat was purchased out of her hard earned money but in the name of her husband.
She has paid EMI through cash or online which was being deposited in the name of her husband.
Her husband started demanding her to release the house etc.
It is also alleged that the petitioners namely husband and in-laws were always demanding money and other valuables etc., and harassing her physically and mentally.
Her husband left her and her three year old daughter and since 11.10.2022 there is no communication.
3. A perusal of the complaint averments would show that there is a matrimonial dispute between the complainant and her husband and family members.
The police have issued notice to the petitioners to participate in the investigation.
The date mentioned in the notice to appear before the police has been lapsed and therefore it is submitted that there is a reasonable apprehension of arrest.
4. As per the submission of the learned counsel, the petitioners are innocent and they have not committed any offence as alleged.
It is submitted that the petitioners are ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation and would regularly attend the court proceedings.
5. In Arnesh Kumar v. The State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273, it is held that there is a phenomenal increase in matrimonial disputes in recent years.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. The State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The institution of marriage is greatly revered in this country.
Section 498-A IPC was introduced with avowed object to combat the menace of harassment to a woman at the hands of her husband and his relatives.
The fact that Section 498-A IPC is a cognizable and non-bailable offence has lent it a dubious place of pride amongst the provisions that are used as weapons rather than shield by disgruntled wives.
The simplest way to harass is to get the husband and his relatives arrested under this provision.

6. Considering that the matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute and the petitioners are not required for any custodial interrogation, the relief sought by the petitioners can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. The petition is allowed.
ii.

The petitioners shall be released in the event of their arrest in Crime No.258/2022 registered at Varthur Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC, subject to following conditions:
(1) Petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of 15 days from the date of receipt of a certified copy of the order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- each [Rupees fifty thousand only]
with two sureties for likesum.
